records.title: rapidoc mcp
records.subtitle: Turn an OpenAPI spec into an MCP server for AI agents: export the project or serve it over stdio.
records.content: mcp export writes the same project as <rapi-doc>'s Export MCP Server button. mcp serve runs it directly, so an agent's config can start it with npx rapidoc mcp serve <spec> (it needs @modelcontextprotocol/sdk installed). Credentials come from the environment, one variable per security scheme; --base-url points the calls at rapidoc mock, and --arazzo adds workflows as tools. EXTERNAL HOSTS (comma-separated, for any) lists the hosts a workflow step's x-operation URL computed at run time may go to, besides those the workflow names.

records.title: rapidoc mock
records.subtitle: Serve an API from its OpenAPI spec, with example or generated responses, request validation and token checks.
records.content: rapidoc mock answers every operation of the spec over HTTP, from its examples or with generated data. It validates requests and can check OAuth tokens against your OpenID Connect issuer. With --stateful it also keeps state: it works out the resources from the spec, starts with generated records, and serves a page at / mock/ui to look inside. It needs @rapidoc/mock. See Mock Server for the options, and the overview for how it compares with the in-browser mock.

records.subtitle: Write the API reference of an OpenAPI spec as a PDF, with your title, colors, fonts and labels.
records.content: rapidoc pdf writes the API reference of a spec as a PDF: a cover page, a table of contents, the security schemes, and every operation with its parameters, request bodies and responses. The spec can be a file or a URL, OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0, and $refs to other files are followed. Without -o the file is named after the spec (openapi.pdf) and written to the current folder. - --schema-style table prints schemas as tables instead of indented object trees, --examples adds request and response examples, and --api-list adds a closing list of every operation. - --no-info, --no-toc, --no-security a

records.title: rapidoc preview
records.subtitle: Show an OpenAPI spec in <rapi-doc> while you edit it, reloading on every change.
records.content: Shows the spec in <rapi-doc> on http://localhost:4000 and reloads it whenever a file in its folder changes, so you can edit the YAML and watch the page. Relative $refs to other files work. --theme picks a <rapi-doc> theme; a URL works too (npx rapidoc preview https://example.com/openapi.json), without reloading.

records.title: 3. Collapse schemas
records.subtitle: Large Specs
records.content: By default, schemas start fully expanded. Large, deeply nested schemas render faster when they start collapsed: - schema-expand-level="1": only the first level of each schema is open; readers expand the rest. - default-schema-tab="schema": request and response bodies open on the schema tab instead of the example tab, so example blocks aren't drawn until a reader opens them.

records.content: File size matters less than structure. Long Markdown descriptions cost little; what slows rendering is the number of operations and how large and deeply nested their schemas are once $refs are resolved. A schema referenced by hundreds of operations is rendered once for each of them.

records.title: Corner Radius (radius)
records.subtitle: Theming Overview
records.content: The radius attribute controls roundness across the entire documentation interface: - radius="none": Sharp 0px corners for brutalist or dense terminal-style layouts. - radius="sm" (default) : Subtle 4px (0.25rem) radius for clean, modern interfaces. - radius="md": Balanced 6px (0.375rem) radius matching contemporary web apps. - radius="lg": Pronounced 8px (0.5rem) radius for playful, consumer-facing portals. - radius="full": Pill-shaped buttons and inputs (9999px) with rounded 8px cards.

records.title: Scaling Factor (scale)
records.subtitle: Theming Overview
records.content: The scale attribute controls typography, base sizing, and proportional margins: - scale="sm": Compact scale (13px base font, 17rem sidebar width). Ideal for embedded documentation cards or split-screen consoles. - scale="default" (default) : Standard desktop scale (14px base font, 18.75rem sidebar width). Optimal for full-page documentation portals. - scale="lg": Generous scale (16px base font, 21rem sidebar width). Optimal for large monitors, accessibility compliance, and presentations.
